scope: All 195 residual West-shaped vse- oblique forms in live v019 Latin sources: 193 vseh, one vsem, and one vsemi, all in base-papers1-43-isv.tex.
choice: Normalize the complete oblique series to the reader's accepted vsi paradigm: vseh to vsih, vsem to vsim, and vsemi to vsimi.
motivation: The reader already uses vsih/vsim/vsimi hundreds of times and its official vśaky/vsi paradigm supplies those forms. The isolated vse- variants duplicate a West-shaped case series inside otherwise identical universal-pronoun contexts. Normalizing them removes morphological inconsistency without changing reference, agreement, syntax, or mathematical content.
alternatives_rejected: Retain both oblique paradigms freely: that leaves a source-layer inconsistency with no semantic distinction.
Normalize the much larger accepted vsi series toward vse-: this would reverse the established house paradigm and broaden the edit needlessly.
Recast each phrase with každy: that would introduce a different determiner family and require agreement changes.

official_dictionary.accepted_entry: id 4326 vśaky, adjective type 1, each/every, with broad East-West-South comparator support

official_pronoun_grammar.relevance: The accepted plural oblique paradigm uses vsih, vsim, and vsimi.

live_corpus_control.finding: All 195 source sites have the same universal-pronoun function as the accepted case series; no protected or semantically distinct occurrence exists.

validation.coverage: 195/195 source sites mapped by exact case-sensitive histogram
validation.protected_spans: TeX comments and foreign-language arguments unchanged
validation.structure: TeX controls, labels/references/citations, braces, math delimiters, byte counts, and line counts unchanged
validation.reproducibility: Frozen output hashes reproduced immediately before atomic apply
